mercy_translation.text:
Perhaps, having heard the prophecy concerning his death, you also wish to learn what was indicated concerning the cross. This too was not passed over in silence; it was made very clear by the holy writers.

Moses first proclaims it beforehand with a loud voice, saying: “You shall see your Life hanging before your eyes, and you will not believe.”

The prophets after him also bear witness concerning this, saying: “I was like an innocent lamb being led to sacrifice, and I did not know it. They devised evil against me, saying: Come, let us put wood into his bread and wipe him out from the land of the living.”

And again: “They pierced my hands and my feet; they counted all my bones. They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots.”

A death suspended in the air and occurring upon wood could be none other than the cross; and in no other kind of death are hands and feet pierced except in the cross alone.

And because, with the Savior's coming, all nations everywhere began to know God, this too was not left without indication. The holy writings remember it: “There shall be the root of Jesse, and the One who rises to rule nations; in him the nations shall hope.” These few things are sufficient as a demonstration of what has taken place.

Yet all Scripture is full of passages refuting Jewish unbelief. For who among the righteous people, holy prophets, and patriarchs recorded in the divine Scriptures received the origin of his body from a virgin alone? Or what woman without a man was sufficient for the generation of a human being? Was not Abel from Adam, Enoch from Jared, Noah from Lamech, Abraham from Terah, Isaac from Abraham, Jacob from Isaac? Was not Judah from Jacob, Moses and Aaron from Amram, Samuel from Elkanah, David from Jesse, Solomon from David, Hezekiah from Ahaz, Josiah from Amon, Isaiah from Amoz, Jeremiah from Hilkiah, Ezekiel from Buzi? Did not each have a father as the source of his human generation? Who, then, was born from a virgin alone? The prophet was deeply concerned to mark this sign.

And before whose birth did a star run ahead in heaven and make the One being born known to the inhabited world? When Moses was born he was hidden by his parents. David's birth was not even heard of by his neighbors; even the great Samuel did not know him but asked whether Jesse had another son. Abraham became known to those nearby only after he had grown great. But the witness of Christ's birth was not a human being: a star appeared in heaven, for the One whose descent was from heaven was also fittingly announced from heaven.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
The scriptural forms follow Athanasius' Septuagintal citations.
Athanasius' genealogical argument is aimed at the uniqueness of the virginal birth in relation to the prophetic signs he cites.
